stage_sentence: Conditions resemble mid-stage 1999. Late-stage triggers — bellwether cracks, insider selling wave — have not fired.

signatures.name: Tightening path steepens
signatures.precedent_1999: The Fed began a 1999-06 tightening cycle, lifting rates six times by 2000-05 from 4.75% to 6.50%.

signatures.name: Fed rhetoric turns hawkish
signatures.threshold_text: fires when rhetoric delta (last 5 vs prior 5 speeches) > +0.4
signatures.precedent_1999: In 2000-02, Greenspan told Congress the economy had excess demand and booming stock prices were a culprit.
signatures.current_reading: Rhetoric delta +0.30 — hawkish drift across last 5 speeches

signatures.name: Estimate revisions turn negative
signatures.threshold_text: fires when median bellwether NTM revision < 0 for 2 consecutive checks
signatures.precedent_1999: Intel warned on 2000-09-22 that Q3 sales would miss forecasts, signaling a broad tech earnings slowdown.
signatures.current_reading: Median bellwether NTM revision +1.8% — still positive

signatures.name: Bellwether guidance cracks
signatures.threshold_text: fires on any strong event: guidance cut/withdrawn or reported miss vs own guidance
signatures.precedent_1999: Intel cut its 3Q sales outlook in 2000-09, and the news sparked a global tech sell-off.
signatures.current_reading: No cuts or withdrawals in the universe this quarter

signatures.name: GPU spot prices rolling over
signatures.threshold_text: fires when H100/B200 spot 30d change < -15% (median of sources)
signatures.precedent_1999: In 2001-06, IDC said DRAM sales would fall 45.7% to $15.7B from $28.9B as prices collapsed.
signatures.current_reading: H100 spot -9% over 30d — drifting, above trigger

signatures.name: Usage-layer churn accelerating
signatures.threshold_text: fires when S1-Q4 destruction >= threshold for 2 consecutive weeks
signatures.precedent_1999: Exodus Communications filed Chapter 11 in 2001-09 after losing customers in the collapsing internet economy.
signatures.current_reading: Startup shutdown mentions up 2 consecutive weeks — cluster forming

signatures.name: Revenue definition drift at labs
signatures.threshold_text: fires on any S1-B1 drift event (metric redefinition in official/press statements)
signatures.precedent_1999: Exodus filed Chapter 11 in 2001-09, a concrete dot-com-era example of business-model and revenue-overbuild drift.
signatures.current_reading: One lab shifted 'ARR' definition to include committed contracts

signatures.name: Vendor-financed revenue material
signatures.threshold_text: fires when Circularity Ratio >= 1% of assets OR Revenue Quality score <= 0.6
signatures.precedent_1999: By 2002-01, the SEC warned that pro forma earnings could mislead investors by obscuring GAAP results.
signatures.current_reading: Circularity Ratio 1.4% of assets — inside the 1999 band

signatures.name: Capex-layer edge distress
signatures.threshold_text: fires on any strong S2-Q5/S2-B1 event touching a registry edge
signatures.precedent_1999: Exodus hit bankruptcy fears in 2001-09 as its customers and network partners were pulled into the telecom collapse.
signatures.current_reading: No canceled or renegotiated registry-edge orders this window

signatures.name: Insider mega-sale wave
signatures.precedent_1999: By mid-2000, insiders at failed telecom names had sold hundreds of millions of dollars of stock before the crash.
signatures.current_reading: 3 mega-sale programs in 90d — below the 4-program trigger

signatures.name: Concentration at record
signatures.precedent_1999: By 2000-12, the S&P 500's top 10 stocks had reached about 23% weight, near the dot-com-era concentration peak.
signatures.current_reading: Top-10 weight 39.4% — above trigger, far above 1999 peak

signatures.name: Breadth divergence extreme
signatures.precedent_1999: In 2000, the market's narrow leadership reversed after the dot-com peak, and the S&P 500 fell into a long lost decade.
signatures.no_data_reason: NYSE 52wk high-low internals not available via You.com/FMP/yfinance free tiers
